Operator CLI (satom)

The satom command-line console for the node itself — read state, run diagnostics and perform privileged repairs, updates and recoveries, even when the web interface is down.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereServer shell — /usr/local/sbin/satom (code in /usr/local/lib/satom-cli/)
On this page
  • Overview
  • Getting the privilege
  • Using it
  • Exit codes
  • Command reference
  • get — read state (any user)
  • show — configuration and reference (any user)
  • diagnose — active probes (any user)
  • execute — change state (root)
  • Examples
  • Application commands (flask)

Overview#

satom is a console tool for the people who run a SATOM node. It is separate from the web interface on purpose: it has to keep working when the web application, its database or the network is broken.

  • Install location: /usr/local/sbin/satom, with its code in /usr/local/lib/satom-cli/. Both are a root-owned copy; the CLI never runs code from /opt/satom.
  • Runs on the system Python (3.10 or later), never on the application's virtual environment, and needs only the standard library to start — so satom diagnose still answers when the virtual environment is broken.
  • Installed by deploy/install-cli.sh, which runs from the installer, after every software update, and on demand with satom execute reinstall cli.
  • Privilege: get, show, diagnose and tree work as any user. Everything under execute (except execute update status) needs root (sudo satom …).

⚠️Warning — Never give the CLI to the service account

A sudo rule that lets the application account run /usr/local/sbin/satom is equivalent to NOPASSWD: ALL. satom diagnose privilege fails if it finds one.

Getting the privilege#

Print the sudoers rule for an operator account (needs no privilege):

satom show sudoers alice

The rule it prints is alice ALL=(root) /usr/local/sbin/satom, to be installed as /etc/sudoers.d/satom-operator with mode 0440 after visudo -cf. Without an account name it uses satomadmin. It also states what the rule grants: everything under execute (service control, venv and unit reinstall, queued code and pip updates, promotion, certificate operations), but no shell.

When an unprivileged user runs a root command, the CLI refuses with permission denied: <command>, shows who you are running as and prints the exact sudo satom … line to use. Exit code 3.

Using it#

satom                       # interactive prompt ('?' lists commands, 'exit' leaves)
satom get system health     # one-shot form, for scripts
satom diagnose ?            # help for one level
satom show tree             # the whole command tree
satom tree execute --root   # only the root commands under execute
Option (anywhere on the line) Effect
--json Machine-readable output, same status and exit code, no colour
--no-color / --color Force colour off / on
--ascii Plain ASCII output for serial consoles
--width N Output width
?, help, -h, --help Help for the current level

An unknown word returns "unknown command", suggestions ("did you mean") and the commands available at that level.

Exit codes#

Code Meaning
0 OK
1 The command ran and the result is bad (unit dead, certificate expired…)
2 Usage error
3 Insufficient privilege
4 Could not run (missing dependency, unreadable credentials)
130 Interrupted

SATOM_CLI_TRACE=1 adds a traceback when a command handler itself crashes.

Command reference#

The console has 121 commands in 44 groups. ! marks commands that change state destructively and ask for --yes.

get — read state (any user)#

Command What it does
get system status Identity, version, HA role and your privilege level
get system health Roll-up of units, /healthz, code freshness and disk. Start here. A web, scheduler or reconciler process that started before the newest code on disk is a warning, with the restart to run
get system performance / interface / disk / time CPU and memory; addresses and ports; disk and growing directories; clock and NTP
get service status [<service>] State of one unit or all
get timer status Timers and .path units: enabled, last and next fire, last result
get node status HA role, peers and peer reachability over :8443
get database status Connection, size, replication
get certificate status / list Served certificate and renewal journal; every certificate on the node
get backup status / list The four backup copies side by side; database bundles for execute restore db
get scheduler status Scheduled actions: what exists, last run, what is overdue
get api versions [<product>] Firmware lines SATOM has API evidence for
get api preflight <appliance\|line> <object> <field>… [--product <p>] Would a payload with these fields be understood on that firmware line?
get device status Per appliance: when its configuration last reached the local store (warning past 26 h, or never), the web console's last reachability probe, and the maintenance flag
get device config [<device> [<section> [<table>]]] [--version <id>] Last harvested configuration, from the local store
get device naming [<device> [--table <type>]] [--product <p>] Naming Discovery from the stored tree: per object type the pattern, how many objects follow it, the exceptions with their reason and the Naming scheme pattern with how many objects match it; without a device, the fleet consensus per product. Needs sudo (it runs the application's analysis as the service account); the device is not contacted
get device not-in-gui <device> [--endpoint <key\|cli path>] Not in GUI, but in CLI for one device: objects only the CLI serves, CLI-only fields of REST objects, REST fields the Fortinet GUI does not show and objects the device's GUI does not draw, each with the channel SATOM writes it over. Needs sudo; the device is not contacted, and field values stay on the page
get signatures status FortiGuard signature DB version and age per FortiWeb (stale past the alert limit, or never updated), the signature source, and what the local signature index holds
get monitor status Probe states and disabled coverage
get job list The job ledger, including ghost jobs
get update history Recent updates and whether the runner picked them up
get release trust Signed releases: the trust anchor (or enforcement OFF), the newest signed commit and whether HEAD's deploy/ matches it. Run with sudo for the signature check; see Signed releases
get git status Branch, drift, unpushed age, parked safety refs
get user list Who can sign in
get alerts status Whether anyone is notified when something breaks
get log <service> [lines] Tail a unit's journal

show — configuration and reference (any user)#

Command What it does
show config The .env, secrets redacted
show units / services Alias → unit map; what each unit is for and which are off limits
show paths / ports / schedule Filesystem layout (replicated or not); listeners; what should run and how often
show privilege / sudoers [<account>] How privilege is split; the sudoers rule to request
show trust Public keys this node accepts, per purpose (update, api_pack, knowledge), with fingerprints
show package <file.tar.gz> Inspect an update package without applying it
show apipack API library packs on the node and what was imported
show knowledge Knowledge packs per lane (age), the feed, the fetch mode and the last fetch
show layouts [<product>] Measured GUI layouts per product and exact build (configuration, live-monitor and "Not in GUI, but in CLI" pages, source packs), and whether each device has a layout for its exact build. Run with sudo: data/ is closed to other accounts
show runbook [<topic>] Offline recovery procedures
show docs [<name>] [<section>] The manual from the local tree (works offline)
show changelog / version Recent release notes; versions of app, CLI and Python
show tree [<prefix>…] [--commands] [--depth N] [--root] [--danger] The whole command tree (also satom tree)

diagnose — active probes (any user)#

all (every check, one exit code), service <service>, install ("is this node armed, or merely installed?" — run on day one), code, scheduler, units, config, data, database, python, network, nginx, certificate, acme, peer, git, updates, privilege, recovery.

💡Tip

diagnose nginx flags a proxied vhost that sends Host $host (which breaks every form behind a non-standard port); execute repair nginx --yes fixes it. See Security model.

💡Tip

diagnose config also shows where a mailed password-reset link points: the node FQDN that replaces any Host header that is not one of the node's names or listed in LINK_HOSTS. It warns when that FQDN is a single label (the link would not resolve off the LAN) or when a LINK_HOSTS entry carries a scheme or a port (it matches no request).

💡Tip

diagnose data fails when data/ is looser than 0750 or anything in the device config vault, the system bundles, the ACME account, the recovery seal or the shared PKI is readable by group or other. Run it with sudo: as an account outside the service group it cannot look, and says so instead of reporting a clean node. execute repair data fixes what it finds — see Data and storage.

execute — change state (root)#

Command What it does
execute restart <service> Restart and verify it came back (for web, waits for /healthz = 200)
execute restart-all Restart the whole stack in order, then check /healthz
execute start / stop <service> Start / stop a service
execute enable / disable <unit> Enable a timer or .path unit / disable a timer (refuses the privileged runner)
execute reload nginx nginx -t, then reload
execute reset theme Re-activate the built-in theme
execute seed actions [--yes] Create the missing rows of the minimum scheduled actions (the same set SATOM creates with a node's first appliance); shows the plan, --yes applies
execute update code [<target>] Queue a git update, or a rollback to a commit
execute update pip <package> <version> Queue an allow-listed package change
execute update package <file.tar.gz> [--yes] [--allow-downgrade] [--no-backup] ! Apply a signed offline update package
execute update fetch [--yes] [--download-only] [--feed <https-url>] ! Download the newest signed package from the upgrade feed and apply it
execute update status [<id>] Latest or a specific update record (any user)
execute reinstall venv ! / units / cli / runner / metrics-store Rebuild a piece of the installation. With a release trust anchor, units, cli, runner and metrics-store install from a root-only copy of the newest signed release, and refuse while deploy/ has unsigned changes
execute sign-release [--yes] ! Primary only. Without --yes, a dry run showing the deploy/ diff since the last signed release; with --yes, adds one signed, empty commit on top of main with the root-only release key and pushes it
execute apipack import <file.tar.gz\|shipped> [--yes] [--product …] [--section …] Import a signed API pack (dry run without --yes)
execute knowledge fetch [--feed <https-url>] [--import] [--yes] Check the knowledge feed; --yes downloads the pack, --import --yes also imports it. Primary only
execute trust add-key <file.pub> [--purpose update\|api_pack\|knowledge] [--name <slug>] / remove-key <name\|fingerprint> [--purpose …] --yes ! Manage signing keys per purpose (default update) — see Pack trust
execute repair permissions / jobs ! / tmp ! / nginx ! Fix drift: file ownership, ghost jobs, scratch files, proxy Host header
execute repair data [--yes] ! Close data/ to other accounts: data/ to 0750, directories under the private trees to 0700, files to 0600. Without --yes it prints the plan and writes nothing. Only removes permission bits, never follows a link, skips an entry replaced between scan and change; a no-op on a clean node. The update runner runs it after every update
execute cert renew Run the certificate renewal pass now
execute alerts run [--dry-run] Evaluate the health checks now
execute backup db / backup git pg_dump into data/system_backups/; git bundle --all
execute restore db <file> --yes ! Replace the database from a bundle (dumps the current one first)
execute admin reset-password <username> Set a password, asked interactively (12 to 1024 characters, the same rule as the web console); written to the audit log as user cli/root
execute admin unlock <username> Clear a lockout; written to the audit log as user cli/root
execute scheduler run / enable / disable <action-id> Fire, enable or disable a scheduled action
execute support bundle Collect diagnostics and journals into one file under /var/tmp/, created exclusively with mode 0600 from its first byte and refusing a name planted as a link
execute device reboot <device> --yes ! / device upgrade <device> --yes ! Run the device's existing action bound to an approved change request
execute maintenance <device> <on\|off> Park or un-park an appliance
execute preflight [<label>] / postflight Health baseline before a risky change; diff after
execute promote ! Promote this standby to primary (--yes)
execute seal recovery ! / unseal recovery ! / export recovery-key [--out PATH] ! Custody of FERNET_KEY and the internal CA key

Service aliases for restart, start and stop: web, scheduler, reconciler, alerts, cert-renew, metrics, datasync, nginx. The privileged updater and postgres are refused on purpose.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: execute admin reset-password and execute admin unlock now write an audit row as user cli/root, and reset-password checks the password with the same 12-character rule as the web console and the installers.

Examples#

🧪Example — Nobody can sign in

satom get user list
sudo satom execute admin unlock admin
sudo satom execute admin reset-password admin

🧪Example — Fresh install, nothing is scheduled

satom diagnose install
sudo satom execute seed actions          # shows the plan
sudo satom execute seed actions --yes    # creates the actions

🧪Example — Close data/ on a node installed by an older release

sudo satom diagnose data                 # lists the entries that are too open
sudo satom execute repair data           # shows the plan, writes nothing
sudo satom execute repair data --yes     # applies it

🧪Example — Update from the release feed

sudo satom execute update fetch --download-only
sudo satom execute update fetch --yes
satom execute update status

See Offline updates.

Application commands (flask)#

Commands that need the application's models run through the Flask CLI, from /opt/satom, as the service account:

cd /opt/satom
sudo -u satom env FLASK_APP=wsgi:app venv/bin/flask <command> --help
Command Purpose
flask create-db Create tables and the first admin (password from SATOM_ADMIN_PASSWORD, or generated to a 0600 file)
flask cert-renew / cert-autopull Node certificate renewal (used by the timer) / one-off pull of an imported certificate
flask alerts-run [--dry-run] [--force] Evaluate and dispatch alerts (used by the timer)
flask preflight [--label] [--out] / postflight [--baseline] [--label] Health baseline and diff
flask canary-restore --device NAME [--apply] [--method] Configuration-restore canary inside the pre/post-flight harness
flask apilib status \| backfill \| import-vendor \| ingest-file \| harvest-fac API library evidence
flask apilib baseline status \| promote \| adopt \| export \| apply \| check \| resolve Endpoint registry baselines
flask apilib pack export \| inspect \| import Signed API packs

See API library and API registry. Flask commands use Click's exit codes (1 on error), not the satom codes above.

Advanced Why the CLI is a copy

/opt/satom belongs to the service account. If sudo satom loaded code from there, a compromised web worker could change what an operator later runs as root. install-cli.sh therefore installs a root:root copy with a system Python, and satom diagnose privilege checks owner, mode and "not a symlink".

The same rule covers what the CLI runs. Anything that executes the application tree — the venv's Python, flask, pip, and git against /opt/satom (git runs programs named in the repository's own configuration) — runs as the service account, never as root. execute reinstall venv builds the venv as that account too. Files the CLI stages under data/ (update packages, API packs) are written by a process that has already dropped privileges, and execute repair permissions never follows a symbolic link.

Advanced The command reference is generated

The command table in the source documentation is generated from deploy/satom_cli/tree.py by deploy/gen_cli_reference.py, and a test fails when it no longer matches. Adding a command is one entry in that tree.

#cli#satom command#naming discovery#signature freshness#gui layouts#code freshness#repair data#diagnose data#file permissions#console#shell#diagnose#execute#get#show#sudo#recovery#update fetch#seed actions#flask#apilib
